findings.where: Screen 9 'Coil against capacitor', more text (and the same line in explain.text)
findings.what: "Textbooks add that Z's angle φ is the angle between the voltage across the parts and the current through them" has no footnote and none of the nine sources supports it; research-notes.md line 835 holds Kirtley's quote "the phase angle between voltage and current is the same as the phase angle of the impedance" (SECONDARY), so cite that, labelled as secondary, or say plainly that the next lesson shows it, and drop "Textbooks add".

The reason the sizes change with f is in explain.text but never reaches the screen, and a steps lesson shows only the frame: a wave twice as steep doubles a coil's voltage for the same current, and drives twice the current through a capacitor for the same voltage. Screens 6 and 13 then reason only from 'f on top' and 'f underneath', so add that one sentence before the formulas.

It goes from 'the voltage's arrow is the current's turned a quarter turn, which is multiplying by j' straight to 'so a coil's opposition points up' without the link that the opposition is what turns the current into the voltage, as R does in V = IR (explain.text has it), and the capacitor gets only 'the other way round' with no i = C dv/dt. Add a clause for each.

The brief's 'Z is not a phasor' sentence and check (brief section 4, Lesson 7) is only in explain.text, which Dan never sees in a steps lesson. Put the sentence on screen 9 or 11, because lesson 8 draws V and I as phasors next to Z.

The brief promises 'every rule here is shown beside its DC twin', but no screen says that with no coil or capacitor Z is just R, his DC resistance, or that parts in series add the way series resistors do; one line would meet the ModEL 'AC is a separate subject' misconception head on.
